+# LUMO Kart — extended courses, rival finish and readable items
+
+This work belongs to the LUMO project and its own development branch. Its source
+baseline is `9f8341494ea316c9e36ed6722915ab34b22e67bd`, from
+`integration/lumo-complete-native-20261114-7a1`.
+
+## Result
+
+The eleven courses following Sonnenhafen now have individually authored routes
+of approximately 1.96–2.04 km, with a continuous themed passage and a real descent
+and ascent in the shared driving curve. Sonnenhafen retains its existing
+1,851.68 m route. Grounded courses travel through covered hills; the sky, city,
+space and laboratory settings use galleries appropriate to their worlds.
+
+The actual runtime rivals have species-specific heads, coats, muzzles, tails and
+suit palettes. Nova's rabbit eyes are smaller and shallower, with seated iris
+surfaces. All fourteen chassis receive additional coachwork, cockpit and wheel
+details while retaining their mechanical anchors and collision dimensions.
+The original imported Lumo character, textures, rig and animations are unchanged.
+
+Three original, solid item emblems replace ambiguous color-only rival orbs:
+gold wind arrow, cyan shield and violet pulse. The same emblems appear together
+on every universal skill gate. The gate does not promise a fixed reward: the
+existing line/speed/drift scoring still chooses it. Road placement stays fixed;
+only descendants animate. Race state now owns the rival effect clock.
+
+## Integration
+
+| Area | Runtime connection |
+|---|---|
+| Routes | `kart_tracks.gd` and `kart_expansion_tracks.gd` supply the authored controls to the existing curve, road sampling, physics and checkpoints. |
+| Passages | `kart_world.gd` builds `AdventureTunnel` in all three world-build branches. The action planner reserves its span before placing kickers, dives or open edges. |
+| Outdoor scenery | Forest clusters, city blocks and expansion scenery follow the longer road. Outdoor dressing skips reserved tunnel spans. |
+| Drivers and chassis | `kart_vehicle.gd` connects the species finish and coachwork helpers before the existing static batching and LOD construction. |
+| Imported future rivals | The real visual adapter validates and instantiates approved local skinned GLBs. Pending roster entries remain disabled. |
+| Items | `kart_island.gd` calls `RESONANCE.advance_ring` and advances each rival FX once per active physics update. Pause, preview, menus and finished races stop that clock. |
+
+The detailed [track handoff](TRACKS.md) contains measured lengths, passage names
+and driving evidence. The [rival asset handoff](RIVAL_ASSET_HANDOFF.md) specifies
+the actual model/rig/animation contract for the separate asset-production team.
+
+## Verified behavior
+
+- All twelve unchanged curve contracts pass: closed seam, road projection,
+  banking, lane separation, curve radius and eight checkpoints.
+- All eleven new worlds build; their passage geometry passes both detail levels,
+  clearance, descent/ascent, action separation and front-face winding checks.
+- Real production physics completed two laps and sixteen ordered checkpoints
+  per course, with zero resets: twenty-four laps and 192 checkpoints in total.
+  The first ten per-course results were completed before that long process was
+  terminated; Desert and Lab passed in a fresh process with a clean final marker.
+- The bounded Godot tunnel raster test passes six interior views with active
+  backface culling, plus six hidden-shell negative controls.
+- Existing item award, use, one-per-lap and save-key behavior passes. Actual
+  island tests also cover exactly one FX update, pause, reduced motion and
+  preservation of banked gate transforms.
+- Held symbols and their hover rail clear the actual rabbit/glider mesh by at
+  least 0.143 m, including the lowest animation bob.
+- All fourteen chassis pass the existing detail/contact gate. The procedural
+  steering test covers 16,280 measurements, with worst glove error 0.278 mm.
+- The original imported Lumo cadence/contact suite passes 1,196 checks. The new
+  rival adapter suite passes 46 checks, including repeated per-frame runtime
+  state calls at 60 and 144 Hz and 30 animation evaluations per second.
+
+These results use Godot 4.6.3 on the local desktop environment. They do not
+establish Android GPU frame time or a newly installed APK. Revised near rival
+geometry costs approximately 9–11% more triangles; distant karts retain their
+batched proxy and omit the new wheel microdetails.
+
+## Visual evidence and reproducibility
+
+The actual product driver/item stage and the tunnel-only review stage use Godot
+framebuffer capture. The tunnel review uses bounded production geometry with
+studio lighting. The latter is distinct from a full race screenshot. Attempts
+to render the complete large world in local software GL ended with signal 9;
+those attempts are not accepted visual or performance evidence.
+
+`scripts/tests/kart_adventure_asset_export.gd` exports and re-imports actual
+visible runtime geometry. Vehicles are static snapshots, not exported rigs or
+new animation systems. Standard PBR materials are retained; unsupported road
+shaders receive a declared portable material approximation in the export
+manifest. Gameplay, collision and procedural animation remain in Godot.
+
+The export copies explicitly convert sRGB vertex colors to linear RGB and retain
+alpha. Exported emissive factors are checked against the source materials and
+written in linear RGB, while their strength and binary geometry chunk are
+preserved. This prevents pale suits, tyres and item accents in Blender without
+altering runtime materials. The color convention follows the
+[glTF 2.0 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html).
+
+Tunnel export uses a real rendering backend: Godot's headless dummy backend does
+not retain usable MultiMesh transform/color readback. The exporter rejects that
+backend for tunnel/all mode before creating output files. Its bounded tunnel
+scene keeps the actual road ribbons, nearby road instances and themed passage;
+instance transforms are checked before writing. The camera and optional studio
+light points are sampled from the existing driving curve. They do not add game
+lighting or alter the course.
+
+```sh
+godot --headless --path . --script res://scripts/tests/kart_adventure_asset_export.gd -- --mode=items --output=/absolute/output/models
+godot --headless --path . --script res://scripts/tests/kart_adventure_asset_export.gd -- --mode=vehicles --output=/absolute/output/models
+python3 tools/run_local_renderer.py --display 120 --output /absolute/output/tunnel-export-qa --timeout 240 -- --script res://scripts/tests/kart_adventure_asset_export.gd -- --mode=tunnel --track-id=crystal_canyon --output=/absolute/output/models
+blender -b --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/art/render_kart_adventure.py -- --input /absolute/output/models --output /absolute/output/blender-items --mode items --samples 96 --animate
+blender -b --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/art/render_kart_adventure.py -- --input /absolute/output/models --output /absolute/output/blender-vehicles --mode vehicles --samples 96
+blender -b --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/art/render_kart_adventure.py -- --input /absolute/output/models --output /absolute/output/blender-tunnel --mode tunnel --track-id=crystal_canyon --samples 64
+```
+
+The isolated renderer command requires an unused display number and a new QA
+output directory. An existing desktop can instead run the export script with
+Godot's normal Compatibility renderer and without `--headless`.
+
+The Blender scenes retain the exported product meshes. Review lighting, cameras,
+floor and display plinths are presentation elements. The optional item loop is
+a studio preview of the real geometry, not a recording of an earned gameplay
+event. Blender files, images, clips and export manifests are supplied separately
+with the review package; the repository contains their reproducible source.
+The item review uses Standard color display for clear hue separation; vehicles
+use AgX. The tunnel uses broad studio lamps, bounded light paths and Blender's
+albedo-guided bilateral compositor to reduce CPU sampling noise while retaining
+part boundaries. This review setup does not change the game's materials or
+lighting. The saved Blender scene includes those settings for inspection.

+# LUMO Kart — rival GLB handoff
+
+**Contract date: 2026-11-14. Target: Godot 4.6.3.** This describes the implemented importer, not a claim that the reference characters have been delivered. The five reference identities are `lion`, `owl`, `rabbit` (Nova), `squirrel` and `turtle`; their current `runtimeReady` flags remain `false`.
+
+Authoritative code: `scripts/games/kart_rival_model_contract.gd`, `kart_rival_visual_adapter.gd`, `lumo_opponent_roster.gd` and `kart_vehicle.gd`. Existing files in `lumo-kart-production/models-final` are static snapshots of the current procedural product geometry. They contain no skins or animation clips and are placement/review references, not replacement driver rigs.
+
+## 1. Coordinates and seated placement
+
+Deliver the character alone at `res://assets/characters/rivals/<id>/driver.glb`. Use metres, **Godot Y up, -Z forward, +X to the driver's right**. The root is already in kart-local space: the adapter adds no automatic scale, translation, turn or standing-to-seated retarget. Keep the character root transform identity and bake any required fitting into the authored asset/rig.
+
+For Blender authoring, `(x, y, z)` in Godot corresponds to `(x, -z, y)` in Blender. Thus the kart's front faces Blender +Y. Export the standard glTF Y-up conversion once; do not apply a second 90-degree correction.
+
+The actual current contact references are:
+
+| Reference | Godot kart-local metres / transform |
+|---|---|
+| Steering-wheel centre | `(0, 1.035, -0.330)` |
+| Wheel rest tilt | X rotation `-0.45` radians |
+| Left/right glove contact centres at rest | `(-0.160, 1.055, -0.340)` / `(0.160, 1.055, -0.340)` |
+| Wheel-local contact points, approximately | `(±0.160, 0.022360, -0.000305)` |
+| Wheel steering | Z rotation `-steer * 0.40`, where `steer` is in `[-1, 1]` |
+| Shoulder joint references | `(±0.290, 1.215, 0.015)` |
+| Boot centres | `(±0.180, 0.800, -0.240)` |
+| Sole centres / bottom | `(±0.180, 0.742, -0.240)` / bottom Y `0.716` |
+| Pedal centres / top | `(±0.180, 0.689, -0.240)` / top Y `0.7115` before the chassis width transform |
+| Seat cushion | Centre `(0, 0.690, 0.070)`; top approximately Y `0.780` |
+| Existing head pivot, for scale reference | `(0, 1.680, 0.070)` |
+
+The authoritative moving hand targets are `steering_wheel.global_transform * wheel_rest_grips[index]`. Pedals belong to `AuroraCoachwork`; some fleet variants scale that parent's X axis, so inspect the actual selected chassis instead of assuming every pedal world X is exactly ±0.180. Keep boots inside the footwell and below the wheel; preserve the clear bonnet and seat envelope.
+
+**Current limitation:** the rival adapter plays authored seated/steering clips. It does not infer hand bones, perform IK, continuously blend steering poses or enforce contact geometrically. Left/right clips are selected when `abs(steer) > 0.30`; otherwise it selects `kart_seated`. Review hands and feet at neutral, partial and full steering before activating a delivery. Machine validation alone does not certify pose fit.
+
+## 2. Rig and animation contract
+
+A GLB must import as a `PackedScene` with a `Node3D` root, at least one genuinely weighted mesh and a local `Skeleton3D`. Bone names are asset-specific: no Lumo bone-name template is imposed. Every animation bone path must resolve to an existing bone in that model's skeleton.
+
+| Clip basename | Required / behaviour |
+|---|---|
+| `kart_seated` | Required; finite positive duration, with at least one keyed skeletal transform track. Frame/time zero must already be a complete seated pose. |
+| `kart_steer_left` | Optional; selected for steering below `-0.30`. |
+| `kart_steer_right` | Optional; selected for steering above `0.30`. |
+| `kart_hit` | Optional; short reaction to a real hit edge, held for at most one second. |
+| `kart_celebrate` | Optional; seated finish celebration. |
+
+A library prefix such as `Rival/kart_seated` is accepted. Put the required and optional clips in the same `AnimationPlayer`. Unknown clips are not selected. Missing or rejected optional clips fall back to `kart_seated`. Keep clips in place: no root movement that pulls the driver out of the vehicle. The adapter can restart a completed selected clip while its state persists; author sustained steering/idle poses and celebrations accordingly.
+
+Accepted enabled tracks are position, rotation and scale 3D tracks plus blend-shape tracks. Paths must remain inside the imported model; each accepted clip must include actual keyed bone animation. Method/value/audio tracks are rejected for selected clips. Scene scripts, collision objects, audio-player nodes and `AnimationTree` are rejected. Imported autoplay is disabled. The vehicle owns the single manual 30 Hz visual clock; pause and reduced-motion state come from the real race.
+
+## 3. Geometry and material delivery
+
+These are the **implemented validation limits**, counted across the entire imported model:
+
+| Limit | Enforced value |
+|---|---:|
+| Triangles | `1…60,000` total; triangle primitives only |
+| Material surfaces | At most `16` total across meshes |
+| Bones | `1…128` per referenced skeleton |
+| Skin binds | `1…128` per skin; each bind resolves to that skeleton |
+| Vertex influences | `4` or `8`; finite non-negative weights summing to `0.98…1.02` per vertex |
+
+Preserve a coherent Lumo material hierarchy: matte coat and cloth, restrained eye gloss, distinct nose/boot finishes. Deliver standard glTF PBR materials and embedded images; retain vertex colours where used. Prefer a shared material atlas and opaque fur over overlapping transparent shells. A practical art target is one 2K base-colour/normal/ORM set per character, but **texture dimensions, embedded-image completeness and visual material quality are not enforced by the current contract**. Review them separately on the target device. A Blender still does not establish Android frame rate.
+
+## 4. Validate a supplied GLB without activating the roster
+
+Run from the project checkout. Import newly delivered files first, then use the real contract directly. The temporary checker below does not change `roster.json` or save any scene:
+
+```bash
+LUMO_PROJECT=/workspace/scratch/a8392560be8d/lumo-kart
+GODOT_BIN=/opt/godot/4.6.3/Godot_v4.6.3-stable_linux.x86_64
+"$GODOT_BIN" --headless --editor --path "$LUMO_PROJECT" --import
+cat > /tmp/lumo_rival_contract_check.gd <<'GDSCRIPT'
+extends SceneTree
+const CONTRACT = preload("res://scripts/games/kart_rival_model_contract.gd")
+func _initialize() -> void:
+	call_deferred("_run")
+func _run() -> void:
+	var paths := OS.get_cmdline_user_args()
+	var passed: bool = not paths.is_empty()
+	for path in paths:
+		if not CONTRACT.model_path_allowed(path) or not ResourceLoader.exists(path, "PackedScene"):
+			print("[RivalGLB] FAIL missing/unbounded asset: ", path)
+			passed = false
+			continue
+		var scene := ResourceLoader.load(path, "PackedScene") as PackedScene
+		if scene == null:
+			print("[RivalGLB] FAIL not a PackedScene: ", path)
+			passed = false
+			continue
+		var model: Node = scene.instantiate()
+		var report: Dictionary = CONTRACT.inspect(model)
+		report.erase("player")
+		report["path"] = path
+		passed = passed and bool(report.get("valid", false))
+		print("[RivalGLB] ", JSON.stringify(report))
+		model.free()
+	if passed:
+		print("[RivalGLB] PASS")
+	quit(0 if passed else 1)
+GDSCRIPT
+python3 "$LUMO_PROJECT/tools/run_godot_probe.py" \
+  --log /tmp/lumo-rival-contract.log --timeout 120 --required '[RivalGLB] PASS' -- \
+  "$GODOT_BIN" --headless --path "$LUMO_PROJECT" \
+  --script /tmp/lumo_rival_contract_check.gd -- \
+  res://assets/characters/rivals/lion/driver.glb \
+  res://assets/characters/rivals/owl/driver.glb \
+  res://assets/characters/rivals/rabbit/driver.glb \
+  res://assets/characters/rivals/squirrel/driver.glb \
+  res://assets/characters/rivals/turtle/driver.glb
+```
+
+Pass one path to check an individual delivery. The current undelivered set is expected to fail this asset check. Existing implementation regressions are `scripts/tests/kart_rival_visual_adapter_regression.gd` and `lumo_opponent_roster_regression.gd`. The adapter regression deliberately checks the current pending roster and uses in-memory fixture rigs; it is not proof that any external reference asset exists.
+
+## 5. Activation, fallback and original Lumo
+
+`runtimeReady:true` alone is insufficient. `lumo_opponent_roster.racing_scene()` also loads and validates the real GLB. `ready_for_race()` requires **exactly five kart identities and all five usable models**. Only then does `kart_island.gd` switch the race's entire opponent roster to lion/owl/rabbit/squirrel/turtle. A partial delivery leaves the existing otter/rabbit/badger/cat/fox field in use. Time-trial and training modes still create no rivals.
+
+Keep undelivered or rejected entries false. After actual import, pose/contact/material review and runtime checks, activate only the delivered entries. Restart the scene/process when changing assets or readiness because the roster and successful validations are cached. A requested imported visual that cannot bind keeps the existing procedural 3D driver visible. A valid import hides that procedural driver and uses a chassis-only distant proxy, so there is one character rather than two overlapping skins.
+
+**Original Lumo is invariant:** do not overwrite, recolour, rescale, rename bones in, re-rig or replace `assets/characters/lumo_animated` or the original Lumo animation adapter. `set_reference_rival_enabled()` explicitly refuses to replace the fox/player Lumo. The static Blender exports are review deliverables; do not install them as rigged opponent assets or claim their review animation is gameplay animation.

+# LUMO Kart: elf erweiterte Strecken und Themenpassagen
+
+Stand: 14. November 2026. Quellbasis: `9f8341494ea316c9e36ed6722915ab34b22e67bd`.
+Dieser Handoff beschreibt den Arbeitsstand im isolierten Branch; er behauptet keine bereits veröffentlichte Version, keinen Merge und keine Android-Freigabe.
+
+## Gemessene Streckenlängen

+
+## Verbundene Themenpassagen
+
+Längen und Abfahrten dieser Tabelle sind auf Millimeter gerundet; die JSON enthält die gespeicherte Präzision, Ein-/Ausstiegsdistanzen und Aufstiege. Die Abfahrt ist die gemessene Höhendifferenz vom Portal zum tiefsten Punkt der echten Fahrkurve innerhalb der Passage.

+
+`hillside` bedeutet eine Fahrbahn unter einer breiten, geschlossenen Hügel-/Felshülle mit verbundenen Portalflächen. Sky, Candy und Galaxy nutzen zur Welt passende überdeckte Galerien; City und Lab haben technisch geformte Hallen. Die Höhe fällt tatsächlich entlang derselben Fahrkurve und steigt zum Ausgang wieder an. Es gibt keine zusätzliche versetzte Fahrbahn oder Teleportation. Die Gewölbe besitzen ein nominelles lokales Mittelprofil von mindestens 9,8 m und seitliche Themendetails: unter anderem Wurzelregale mit Büchern, Tempelzeichen, Kristalle, Basalt-/Glutbänder, Säulen, Zuckerornamente, Moleküle und Planeten.
+
+## Geometrie und Integration
+
+- `scripts/games/kart_adventure_routes.gd` enthält die elf eigenständig definierten Kontrollpunktfolgen und Portalanker. `kart_tracks.gd` und `kart_expansion_tracks.gd` liefern sie über den bestehenden Katalog.
+- `kart_world.gd::_make_curve()` bleibt die gemeinsame Autorität für Fahrbahn, Bankwinkel, Projektion, Leitplanken und acht Kontrollpunkte. `kart_adventure_tunnels.gd` baut daran die Innenhülle, Außenhaut, Portale und gebündelte Details. Der Tunnel fügt keine `CollisionObject3D` hinzu.
+- `world.adventure_tunnel` steht nach `_make_curve()` bereit. Der erzeugte `AdventureTunnel`-Knoten und die Welt tragen identische `adventure_tunnel`-Metadaten mit `start_m`, `end_m`, `length_m`, `name`, `theme`, `covered_type`, `descent_m`, `clearance_m` und Geometriezählungen. Der Plan steht außerdem unter `adventure_tunnel_plan`.
+- `kart_action_course.gd` reserviert die Tunnelspannen einschließlich bestehendem Sicherheitsabstand. Die deterministische Suche kann auf langen Strecken weiter ausweichen; Start/Ziel-, Sprung-, Loop-, Kicker-, Slalom- und Tauchstreckenbedingungen bleiben erhalten. Der Test prüft auch die fest gesetzten Sprünge und Loops gegen die Tunnelspannen.
+- Die Innenflächen verwenden Godots Uhrzeigersinn als Vorderseite; die beabsichtigte Beleuchtungsnormale bleibt erhalten. Portalnormalen zeigen nach außen. Backface-Culling bleibt eingeschaltet.
+- Outdoor-Kits, Fleet-Möbel und Expansion-Landmarken meiden die reservierten Passagen; überlappende alte Tunnel-/Brücken-/Tor-Dekoration wird ausgespart. Materialien, Formmeshes und MultiMesh-Infrastruktur stammen weiterhin aus dem vorhandenen Weltaufbau.
+
+## Dichte und Weltgrenzen
+
+Der Zauberwald verteilt seine Cluster entlang der neuen Kurve statt im alten ±100-m-Feld. Es gibt 180/300 deterministische Platzierungsversuche für niedrige/hohe Detailstufe; Straßen-, Wasser- und Bibliothekskonflikte werden verworfen. Der neue Geometrievertrag verlangt mindestens 80 erhaltene Cluster, Bedeckung aller acht Streckenachtel und freien Kronenumraum zur Fahrbahn und Bibliothek.
+
+Holo-City ergänzt 60/96 geprüfte Boulevardblöcke als Platzierungsversuche und setzt seine äußere Skyline relativ zur neuen Weltausdehnung. Die Terrainränder von Zauberwald und City bekommen 48 m statt 18 m Zugabe. Sonnenhafens Randberechnung bleibt unverändert. Expansion-Landmarken verwenden ungefähr 30/17 m Abstand bei höchstens 76/128 Versuchen; die vorhandene 900 × 900 m Bodenfläche bleibt bestehen. Der Test prüft, dass Kurve plus 29-m-Hügelhalbbreite innerhalb dieser Fläche liegen.
+
+Die historische Bibliotheksregression bleibt auf der ursprünglichen 376-m-Waldroute als festem Vergleichsfall erhalten: sämtliche bisherigen Zufalls-, Identitäts-, Freiraum- und Entfernungsbedingungen bleiben aktiv. Die absichtlich neu verteilte Adventure-Vegetation wird separat im aktuellen Geometrievertrag geprüft.
+
+## Tatsächliche Validierung und Grenzen
+
+| Prüfung | Beobachtetes Ergebnis |
+| --- | --- |
+| `kart_track_contract.gd` | 12/12 Strecken bestanden: Naht, Projektion, acht Kontrollpunkte, Bankrahmen, Trennung anderer Streckenabschnitte und ursprünglicher Mindestradius >18 m. Kleinster gemessener Radius der elf neuen Kurse: 60,2 m. |
+| `kart_adventure_regression.gd` | 11/11 vollständige Welten in niedriger Detailstufe aufgebaut; jeder Tunnel zusätzlich in hoher Geometriedichte geprüft. Spannen, Höhenprofil, Action-Abstand, Weltgrenzen, Freiraum, Polygon-Winding und Waldabdeckung bestanden. Dies ist kein vollständiger High-Detail-Welt-Render. |
+| `kart_track_theme_world_regression.gd` | Alle elf Welten in niedriger Detailstufe: 793 Prüfungen und 282 echte Geometrie-Stützproben bestanden. |

+static func layout(world) -> Dictionary:
+	if not ROUTES.supports(str(world.track_id)) or not world.definition.has("adventure"):
+		return {}
+	var profile: Dictionary = ROUTES.profile(str(world.track_id))
+	var first: int = int(profile.entry_index)
+	var last: int = int(profile.exit_index)
+	var start: float = world.curve.get_closest_offset(world.curve.get_point_position(first))
+	var finish: float = world.curve.get_closest_offset(world.curve.get_point_position(last))
+	var minimum: float = INF
+	for index in range(65):
+		minimum = minf(minimum, world.curve.sample_baked(lerpf(start, finish, float(index) / 64.0), true).y)

+	var exit_height: float = world.curve.sample_baked(finish, true).y

+	result.merge({

+		"start_m": start, "end_m": finish, "length_m": finish - start,
+		"clearance_m": SHOULDER + ROOF, "half_width_m": HALF_WIDTH,

+		"floor_min_m": minimum, "descent_m": entry_height - minimum,
+		"ascent_m": exit_height - minimum,

+static func build(world) -> void:

+static func cross_section(world, distance: float, segments: int) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var at: Vector3 = world.position_at(distance)
+	var basis: Basis = world.frame(distance)
+	var theme: String = str(world.adventure_tunnel.theme)
+	var points := PackedVector3Array([at - basis.x * HALF_WIDTH + basis.y * FOOT])
+	for index in range(segments + 1):
+		var angle: float = PI * (1.0 - float(index) / segments)
+		var x: float = cos(angle) * HALF_WIDTH
+		var y: float = SHOULDER + sin(angle) * ROOF
+		if theme in ["city", "lab"]:
+			# A broad, bevelled transit/laboratory gallery, distinct from the caves.
+			y = SHOULDER + minf(1.0, sin(angle) * 1.35) * ROOF
+		elif theme == "sky":
+			y += pow(sin(angle), 5.0) * 1.4
+		elif theme in ["crystal", "volcano", "forest", "jungle"]:
+			# Outward-only relief retains the complete smooth driving envelope.
+			var relief: float = 0.15 + 0.30 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(distance * 0.11 + index * 1.7))
+			x *= 1.0 + relief * 0.025
+			y += relief * sin(angle)

+	points.append(at + basis.x * HALF_WIDTH + basis.y * FOOT)
+	return points

+static func _outer(world, distance: float, inner: Vector3) -> Vector3:
+	var basis: Basis = world.frame(distance)

+	var local: Vector3 = basis.inverse() * (inner - at)
+	local.x *= 1.11
+	local.y += 0.85

+## Contract for authored seated rival GLBs. No retargeting or generated stand-ins.
+## Geometry uses Godot metres, Y up, -Z forward, and the kart's local seat space.
+const MAX_TRIANGLES := 60000
+const MAX_BONES := 128
+const MAX_SURFACES := 16
+const CLIPS := ["kart_seated", "kart_steer_left", "kart_steer_right", "kart_hit", "kart_celebrate"]
+
+
+static func model_path_allowed(path: String) -> bool:
+	return path.begins_with("res://assets/characters/rivals/") and path.ends_with(".glb") and not ".." in path
+
+
+static func _belongs_to(node: Node, model: Node) -> bool:
+	return node != null and (node == model or model.is_ancestor_of(node))
+
+
+static func _safe_clip(player: AnimationPlayer, animation: Animation, model: Node3D) -> bool:
+	if animation == null or animation.length <= 0.0 or not is_finite(animation.length):
+		return false
+	var origin: Node = player.get_node_or_null(player.root_node)
+	if not _belongs_to(origin, model):
+		return false
+	var tracks := 0
+	var skeletal_track := false
+	for index in range(animation.get_track_count()):
+		if not animation.track_is_enabled(index):
+			continue
+		var kind: int = animation.track_get_type(index)
+		if kind not in [Animation.TYPE_POSITION_3D, Animation.TYPE_ROTATION_3D, Animation.TYPE_SCALE_3D, Animation.TYPE_BLEND_SHAPE]:
+			return false
+		var path: NodePath = animation.track_get_path(index)
+		var target: Node = origin.get_node_or_null(NodePath(path.get_concatenated_names()))
+		if not _belongs_to(target, model):
+			return false
+		if kind == Animation.TYPE_BLEND_SHAPE:
+			if not target is MeshInstance3D or path.get_subname_count() != 1:
+				return false
+		elif target is Skeleton3D:
+			if path.get_subname_count() != 1 or target.find_bone(str(path.get_subname(0))) < 0:
+				return false
+			skeletal_track = skeletal_track or animation.track_get_key_count(index) > 0
+		elif not target is Node3D or path.get_subname_count() != 0:
+			return false
+		tracks += animation.track_get_key_count(index)

+static func _valid_skin(part: MeshInstance3D, skeleton: Skeleton3D) -> bool:
+	var binds: int = part.skin.get_bind_count()
+	if binds < 1 or binds > MAX_BONES:
+		return false
+	for bind in range(binds):
+		var named: StringName = part.skin.get_bind_name(bind)
+		var bone: int = skeleton.find_bone(str(named)) if not str(named).is_empty() else part.skin.get_bind_bone(bind)

+			return false
+	for surface in range(part.mesh.get_surface_count()):
+		var arrays: Array = part.mesh.surface_get_arrays(surface)
+		if arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_BONES] == null or arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS] == null:
+			return false
+		var bones: PackedInt32Array = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_BONES]
+		var weights: PackedFloat32Array = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_WEIGHTS]
+		var vertices: int = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_VERTEX].size()

+		var stride: int = bones.size() / vertices

+			for influence in range(stride):

+func _portable_material(source: Material, tint: Color = Color.WHITE) -> Material:
+	if source is StandardMaterial3D:
+		if tint == Color.WHITE:
+			return source
+		# Keep the source Resource as the key, and all RGBA components exactly.
+		# Shared instance colours must not create thousands of duplicate materials.
+		if not tinted_portable_materials.has(source):
+			tinted_portable_materials[source] = {}
+		var variants: Dictionary = tinted_portable_materials[source]
+		var tint_key := Vector4(tint.r, tint.g, tint.b, tint.a)
+		if variants.has(tint_key):
+			return variants[tint_key]
+		var copy: StandardMaterial3D = source.duplicate()
+		copy.albedo_color *= tint
+		variants[tint_key] = copy
+		return copy
+	var material := StandardMaterial3D.new()
+	material.albedo_color = tint
+	material.vertex_color_use_as_albedo = true
+	material.roughness = 0.65
+	if source is ShaderMaterial:
+		var road_color = source.get_shader_parameter("road_tint")
+		if road_color is Color:
+			material.albedo_color *= road_color
+		var identifier: String = source.shader.resource_path if source.shader != null else "unnamed_shader"
+		translated_materials[identifier] = "portable PBR approximation; runtime shader remains in Godot"
+	return material

+func _assert_material_values(actual: Array, expected: Array) -> void:
+	assert(actual.size() == expected.size())
+	for index in range(actual.size()):
+		assert(absf(float(actual[index]) - float(expected[index])) <= 0.000001, "glTF material differs from the runtime material")

+func _linearize_export_vertex_colors(state: GLTFState) -> int:
+	# Godot's runtime shader decodes sRGB vertex colours when this flag is set.
+	# glTF COLOR_0 is linear. Convert only the exporter-owned ImporterMesh arrays:
+	# this also avoids quantizing linear colours through an 8-bit ArrayMesh again.
+	# Scene/runtime mesh buffers, material flags, geometry and alpha stay untouched.
+	# GLTFState.materials is populated only during serialization. At this stage
+	# each ImporterMesh surface carries the actual active instance material.
+	var converted_surfaces := 0
+	for entry: GLTFMesh in state.get_meshes():
+		var source: ImporterMesh = entry.get_mesh()
+		if source == null:
+			continue
+		var overrides: Array[Material] = entry.get_instance_materials()
+		var active_materials: Array[Material] = []
+		var key: String = str(source.get_instance_id())
+		for surface in range(source.get_surface_count()):
+			var active: Material = source.get_surface_material(surface)
+			if surface < overrides.size() and overrides[surface] != null:
+				active = overrides[surface]
+			active_materials.append(active)
+			key += ":" + str(active.get_instance_id() if active != null else 0)
+		if linear_vertex_meshes.has(key):
+			var cached: Dictionary = linear_vertex_meshes[key]
+			entry.set_mesh(cached.mesh)
+			entry.set_instance_materials(cached.materials)
+			converted_surfaces += int(cached.surfaces)
+			continue
+		var copy := ImporterMesh.new()
+		copy.set_blend_shape_mode(source.get_blend_shape_mode())
+		for shape in range(source.get_blend_shape_count()):
+			copy.add_blend_shape(source.get_blend_shape_name(shape))
+		var count := 0
+		var portable_materials: Array[Material] = []
+		for surface in range(source.get_surface_count()):
+			var arrays: Array = source.get_surface_arrays(surface)
+			var material: Material = active_materials[surface]
+			if material is StandardMaterial3D and material.vertex_color_use_as_albedo and material.vertex_color_is_srgb:
+				var material_key: int = material.get_instance_id()
+				if not linear_vertex_materials.has(material_key):
+					var portable: StandardMaterial3D = material.duplicate()
+					portable.vertex_color_is_srgb = false
+					linear_vertex_materials[material_key] = portable
+				material = linear_vertex_materials[material_key]
+				if arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_COLOR] != null:
+					var colors: PackedColorArray = arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_COLOR].duplicate()
+					for vertex in range(colors.size()):
+						var original: Color = colors[vertex]
+						colors[vertex] = original.srgb_to_linear()
+						colors[vertex].a = original.a
+					arrays[Mesh.ARRAY_COLOR] = colors
+					count += 1
+			portable_materials.append(material)
+			var shapes: Array[Array] = []
+			for shape in range(source.get_blend_shape_count()):
+				shapes.append(source.get_surface_blend_shape_arrays(surface, shape))
+			var lods: Dictionary = {}
+			for lod in range(source.get_surface_lod_count(surface)):
+				lods[source.get_surface_lod_size(surface, lod)] = source.get_surface_lod_indices(surface, lod)
+			copy.add_surface(source.get_surface_primitive_type(surface), arrays, shapes, lods,
+				material, source.get_surface_name(surface), source.get_surface_format(surface))
+		linear_vertex_meshes[key] = {"mesh": copy, "materials": portable_materials, "surfaces": count}
+		entry.set_mesh(copy)
+		entry.set_instance_materials(portable_materials)
+		converted_surfaces += count
+	return converted_surfaces
+

+func _correct_serialized_emission(path: String, state: GLTFState) -> Dictionary:
+	# Godot 4.6.3 serializes emission with linear_to_srgb(), while the authored
+	# palette uses sRGB colours. Write glTF's linear factors from those exact
+	# source colours. Keep emission strength and every binary byte unchanged.
+	var original: PackedByteArray = FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes(path)
+	assert(original.size() >= 20 and original.decode_u32(0) == 0x46546c67)
+	assert(original.decode_u32(4) == 2 and original.decode_u32(8) == original.size())
+	var json_size: int = original.decode_u32(12)
+	assert(original.decode_u32(16) == 0x4e4f534a and json_size % 4 == 0)
+	assert(20 + json_size <= original.size())
+	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(original.slice(20, 20 + json_size).get_string_from_utf8())
+	assert(parsed is Dictionary)
+	var document: Dictionary = parsed
+	var serialized: Array = document.get("materials", [])
+	var sources: Array[Material] = state.get_materials()
+	assert(serialized.size() == sources.size(), "Export material indices must match GLTFState")
+	var corrected := 0
+	for index in range(sources.size()):
+		var source: Material = sources[index]
+		if not source is StandardMaterial3D or not source.emission_enabled:
+			continue
+		var previous: Array = serialized[index].get("emissiveFactor", [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
+		var emitted: Color = source.emission.linear_to_srgb()
+		assert(previous.size() == 3 and absf(float(previous[0]) - emitted.r) < 0.00001
+			and absf(float(previous[1]) - emitted.g) < 0.00001 and absf(float(previous[2]) - emitted.b) < 0.00001,
+			"Serialized material index must match the source emission before correction")
+		var color: Color = source.emission.srgb_to_linear()
+		assert(is_finite(color.r) and is_finite(color.g) and is_finite(color.b))
+		assert(minf(color.r, minf(color.g, color.b)) >= 0.0 and maxf(color.r, maxf(color.g, color.b)) <= 1.0,
+			"Authored emission factors must be bounded; brightness uses emission_energy_multiplier")
+		serialized[index]["emissiveFactor"] = [color.r, color.g, color.b]
+		corrected += 1
+	var binary_chunk: PackedByteArray = original.slice(20 + json_size)
+	var binary_hash: String = _bytes_sha256(binary_chunk)
+	if corrected == 0:
+		return {"materials_corrected": 0, "binary_chunk_unchanged": true,
+			"binary_sha256_before": binary_hash, "binary_sha256_after": binary_hash}
+	var json_bytes: PackedByteArray = JSON.stringify(_native_glb_numbers(document), "", false, true).to_utf8_buffer()
+	while json_bytes.size() % 4 != 0:
+		json_bytes.append(0x20)
+	var header := PackedByteArray()
+	header.resize(20)
+	header.encode_u32(0, 0x46546c67)
+	header.encode_u32(4, 2)
+	header.encode_u32(8, 20 + json_bytes.size() + binary_chunk.size())
+	header.encode_u32(12, json_bytes.size())
+	header.encode_u32(16, 0x4e4f534a)
+	var packed: PackedByteArray = header + json_bytes + binary_chunk
+	assert(packed.slice(20 + json_bytes.size()) == binary_chunk)
+	var temporary: String = path + ".color-tmp"
+	var file := FileAccess.open(temporary, FileAccess.WRITE)
+	assert(file != null)
+	file.store_buffer(packed)
+	file.close()
+	assert(DirAccess.rename_absolute(temporary, path) == OK)
+	var verified: PackedByteArray = FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes(path)
+	var after_hash: String = _bytes_sha256(verified.slice(20 + verified.decode_u32(12)))
+	assert(after_hash == binary_hash)
+	return {"materials_corrected": corrected, "binary_chunk_unchanged": true,
+		"binary_sha256_before": binary_hash, "binary_sha256_after": after_hash}
+
+
+func _bytes_sha256(value: PackedByteArray) -> String:
+	var context := HashingContext.new()
+	assert(context.start(HashingContext.HASH_SHA256) == OK)
+	assert(context.update(value) == OK)
+	return context.finish().hex_encode()
+
+
+func _native_glb_numbers(value: Variant) -> Variant:
+	# Godot JSON parsing represents every JSON number as a float. Restore
+	# integral values so indices remain usable by strict glTF importers.
+	if value is Dictionary:
+		var result: Dictionary = {}
+		for key in value:
+			result[key] = _native_glb_numbers(value[key])
+		return result
+	if value is Array:
+		var result: Array = []
+		for item in value:
+			result.append(_native_glb_numbers(item))
+		return result
+	if value is float and is_finite(value) and absf(value) <= 9007199254740991.0 and value == floor(value):
+		return int(value)
+	return value
+
+
+func _vector(value: Vector3) -> Array[float]:
+	return [value.x, value.y, value.z]

+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=("vehicles", "items", "tunnel"), required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=96)
+    parser.add_argument("--animate", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--all-views", action="store_true", help="Render every individual kart as well as the fleet")
+    parser.add_argument("--track-id", default="crystal_canyon")
+    return parser.parse_args(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:])
+

+def material(name, color, metallic=0.0, roughness=0.4):
+    result = bpy.data.materials.new(name)
+    result.use_nodes = True
+    bsdf = result.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
+    bsdf.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (*color, 1.0)
+    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metallic
+    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = roughness
+    return result
+
+
+def aim(obj, point):
+    obj.rotation_euler = (Vector(point) - obj.location).to_track_quat("-Z", "Y").to_euler()
+
+
+def area(name, at, target, watts, size, color=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)):
+    data = bpy.data.lights.new(name, "AREA")
+    data.energy = watts
+    data.shape = "DISK"
+    data.size = size
+    data.color = color
+    light = bpy.data.objects.new(name, data)
+    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(light)
+    light.location = at
+    aim(light, target)
+    return light
+
+
+def camera(at, target, lens=52.0):
+    data = bpy.data.cameras.new("LUMO_ReviewCamera")
+    data.lens = lens
+    data.clip_end = 4000.0
+    data.dof.use_dof = False
+    obj = bpy.data.objects.new("LUMO_ReviewCamera", data)
+    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)
+    obj.location = at
+    aim(obj, target)
+    bpy.context.scene.camera = obj
+    return obj

+    scene.cycles.device = "CPU"

+    scene.cycles.use_adaptive_sampling = True
+    scene.cycles.adaptive_threshold = 0.012

+    scene.cycles.diffuse_bounces = 4
+    scene.cycles.glossy_bounces = 4

+    scene.render.resolution_y = 1200
+    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100
+    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = "PNG"
+    scene.render.image_settings.color_mode = "RGBA"

+    scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("LUMO_StudioWorld")
+    scene.world.use_nodes = True

+def import_asset(path, name, normalize=True):
+    before = set(bpy.data.objects)
+    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=str(path))
+    objects = set(bpy.data.objects) - before
+    assert any(obj.type == "MESH" for obj in objects), f"No geometry in {path}"
+    group = bpy.data.objects.new(name, None)
+    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(group)
+    group["source_glb"] = path.name
+    group["source_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+    group["geometry_source"] = "LUMO Kart runtime export"
+    for obj in objects:
+        if obj.parent not in objects:
+            obj.parent = group
+    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
+    if normalize:
+        bounds = [obj.matrix_world @ Vector(corner)
+                  for obj in objects if obj.type == "MESH" for corner in obj.bound_box]
+        minimum = Vector(tuple(min(v[i] for v in bounds) for i in range(3)))
+        maximum = Vector(tuple(max(v[i] for v in bounds) for i in range(3)))
+        group.location = (-(minimum.x + maximum.x) * 0.5,
+                          -(minimum.y + maximum.y) * 0.5, -minimum.z)
+    return group, objects
+

+def visibility(objects, visible):

+        obj.hide_render = not visible

+def render(scene, path):
+    scene.render.filepath = str(path)
+    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
+    assert path.is_file() and path.stat().st_size > 1000
+    print("LUMO_RENDER", path.name, flush=True)

+def pack_and_save(path):
+    for image in bpy.data.images:
+        if image.source == "FILE" and not image.packed_file:
+            image.pack()
+    for screen in bpy.data.screens:
+        for space in screen.areas:
+            if space.type == "VIEW_3D":
+                space.spaces.active.shading.type = "SOLID"
+                space.spaces.active.shading.color_type = "MATERIAL"
+                space.spaces.active.region_3d.view_perspective = "CAMERA"
+    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=str(path), compress=True)

+        plinth.data.materials.append(material("LUMO_Plinth_" + kind, (0.035, 0.055, 0.088), 0.55, 0.27))

+        frame_dir = args.output / "item-frames"
+        frame_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        scene.frame_start = 1
+        scene.frame_end = 48
+        for frame in range(49):
+            phase = frame * math.tau / 48
+            for index, (group, base, _) in enumerate(groups):
+                local_phase = phase + index * 0.7
+                group.location.z = base.z + math.sin(local_phase * 2.0) * 0.045
+                group.rotation_euler.z = math.sin(local_phase) * 0.22
+                group.keyframe_insert(data_path="location", frame=frame + 1)
+                group.keyframe_insert(data_path="rotation_euler", frame=frame + 1)
+        for action in bpy.data.actions:
+            for curve in action.fcurves:
+                for key in curve.keyframe_points:
+                    key.interpolation = "LINEAR"
+        for frame in range(1, 49):

+def godot_to_blender(value):
+    return Vector((value[0], -value[2], value[1]))

+def configure_tunnel_review(scene):
+    # The passage is a bounded studio review. Broad lamps illuminate it;
+    # the small emissive game decorations remain visible without acting as
+    # thousands of sampled lights. No source palette or mesh is changed.
+    for source_material in bpy.data.materials:
+        source_material.cycles.emission_sampling = "NONE"
+    scene.cycles.sample_clamp_indirect = 0.5
+    scene.cycles.sample_clamp_direct = 1.0
+    scene.cycles.max_bounces = 2
+    scene.cycles.diffuse_bounces = 2
+    scene.cycles.glossy_bounces = 1
+    scene.cycles.blur_glossy = 1.0
+    # This Blender build has no usable Cycles denoiser. Its native bilateral
+    # compositor uses the clean albedo pass to preserve edges between parts.
+    bpy.context.view_layer.use_pass_diffuse_color = True
+    scene.use_nodes = True
+    nodes = scene.node_tree.nodes
+    nodes.clear()
+    layers = nodes.new("CompositorNodeRLayers")
+    guide = layers.outputs.get("DiffCol") or layers.outputs.get("Diffuse Color")
+    assert guide is not None, "The albedo guide pass must exist"
+    filtered = nodes.new("CompositorNodeBilateralblur")
+    filtered.name = "LUMO_AlbedoGuidedStudioFilter"
+    filtered.iterations = 2
+    filtered.sigma_space = 4.0
+    filtered.sigma_color = 0.1
+    result = nodes.new("CompositorNodeComposite")
+    scene.node_tree.links.new(layers.outputs["Image"], filtered.inputs["Image"])
+    scene.node_tree.links.new(guide, filtered.inputs["Determinator"])
+    scene.node_tree.links.new(filtered.outputs["Image"], result.inputs["Image"])

+def tunnel(args, scene):
+    manifest = json.loads((args.input / "manifest-tunnel.json").read_text())
+    record = next(row for row in manifest["models"] if row.get("track") == args.track_id)
+    import_asset(args.input / record["file"], "LUMO_AdventureTunnel", normalize=False)
+    eye = godot_to_blender(record["camera"])
+    target = godot_to_blender(record["target"])
+    view = camera(eye, target, 25.0)
+    # Match the reviewed Godot driver's view, including road banking and the
+    # vertical field of view, rather than guessing a photographic lens.
+    up = godot_to_blender(record["camera_up"]).normalized()
+    forward = (target - eye).normalized()
+    right = forward.cross(up).normalized()
+    assert right.length > 0.99
+    up = right.cross(forward).normalized()
+    view.rotation_mode = "QUATERNION"
+    view.rotation_quaternion = Matrix((right, up, -forward)).transposed().to_quaternion()
+    view.data.sensor_fit = "VERTICAL"
+    view.data.sensor_height = 24.0
+    view.data.lens = view.data.sensor_height / (2.0 * math.tan(math.radians(record["vertical_fov_degrees"]) * 0.5))
+    area("LUMO_PortalSoftlight", eye + Vector((0, 0, 7)), target, 3500, 9.0)
+    area("LUMO_GalleryFill", target + Vector((0, 0, 3)), target - Vector((0, 0, 2)), 1800, 6.0,
+         (0.65, 0.83, 1.0))
+    for index, point in enumerate(record["review_light_points"]):
+        area(f"LUMO_ReviewInterior_{index + 1:02d}", godot_to_blender(point["position"]),
+             godot_to_blender(point["target"]), 1200, 8.0, (0.86, 0.91, 1.0))
+    sun_data = bpy.data.lights.new("LUMO_Daylight", "SUN")
+    sun_data.energy = 2.0
+    sun_data.angle = math.radians(12)
+    sun = bpy.data.objects.new("LUMO_Daylight", sun_data)
+    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(sun)
+    sun.rotation_euler = (math.radians(25), math.radians(-24), math.radians(36))
+    scene.render.resolution_x = 1920
+    scene.render.resolution_y = 1080
+    configure_tunnel_review(scene)
+    render(scene, args.output / ("LUMO_Tunnel_" + args.track_id + ".png"))
+    pack_and_save(args.output / ("LUMO_Tunnel_" + args.track_id + ".blend"))

+def main():
+    args = arguments()
+    args.input = args.input.resolve()
+    args.output = args.output.resolve()
+    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    assert args.samples > 0
+    scene = setup(args.samples)
+    {"vehicles": vehicles, "items": items, "tunnel": tunnel}[args.mode](args, scene)
+    meshes = [obj for obj in scene.objects if obj.type == "MESH"]
+    triangles = 0
+    for obj in meshes:
+        obj.data.calc_loop_triangles()
+        triangles += len(obj.data.loop_triangles)
+    report = {
+        "blender": bpy.app.version_string, "renderer": "Cycles CPU", "mode": args.mode,
+        "source": "verified exported LUMO runtime GLBs", "product_geometry_redesigned_in_render": False,
+        "presentation": "studio lights/camera/floor; source gameplay geometry unchanged",
+        "meshes_in_review_scene": len(meshes), "base_mesh_triangles_in_review_scene": triangles,
+        "animation": (
+            "four-second studio loop of product item geometry"
+            if args.mode == "items" and args.animate else "static review"

+    print("LUMO_BLENDER_PASS", json.dumps({"mode": args.mode, "meshes": len(meshes), "triangles": triangles}), flush=True)
